audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart claimed Jax at Levels 1, 2, 6 and first item, but every 'why' string on the same rows describes Aatrox winning those stages (his sweetspot Q into Infernal Chains, his drain-trade, his healing item out-draining first-item Jax). The packet levelChart also reads Skill/Aatrox/Aatrox/Aatrox/Skill/Aatrox/Jax.
audit.why: Jax at 51.23% over 1917 games is an even lane won late, not an early-lane win. Aatrox owns levels 2-5 with Q sweetspot + W lock; Jax only takes over at two items.
audit.corrected: Level 1 Skill, Levels 2-5 Aatrox, Level 6 Skill (both ults flip it), first item Aatrox, two items Jax.

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's R was written as 'Grandmaster’s Might' in phases[4].why and breakdown.late, while the content layer uses Grandmaster at Arms.
audit.why: One champion, two ult names across the same page. The mirror audit (aatrox vs jax) states Grandmaster-at-Arms (R), 110s.
audit.corrected: Grandmaster at Arms throughout. Spikes: Jax R at 6 (110/100/90s Armor/MR burst), Trinity Force, then the two-item side-lane window. Aatrox: W online at 2, World Ender at 6 (120/100/80s), healing item.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page states that Infernal Chains grounds — and Jax's Q and W are both flagged dashes.
audit.why: Aatrox W carries the grounding flag: caught in the Chains area, Jax cannot Leap Strike in or out, which is exactly why he must hold Counter Strike for that window rather than for the Q sweetspot alone.
audit.corrected: Infernal Chains (W, 20s at rank 1) grounds — inside it Leap Strike is dead, so E is the only out. Counter Strike (E, 17s at rank 1) dodges the Q swings and the empowered-auto but must be spent on his recommit, not on empty air.
sources: enemyKit W flags: grounding, slow, zone

audit.why: World Ender at 120s rank 1 is the punishable cooldown and the page already tracks it before every commit.

audit.whatIsWrong: The three flagged suspectNames are false positives.
audit.why: 'World Ender's', 'Hold Counter Strike' and 'Counter Strike's' are all the real Riot names with possessives/verbs attached.

edits.after: His sweetspot Q knockup into Infernal Chains locks you for Q2/Q3 before Counter Strike (17s) pays off. Take short trades.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Aatrox must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: His drain-trade grinds you down if the fight runs long. Keep the wave near your side and trade in short bursts, never extended.

edits.before: Grandmaster’s Might stats win every extended duel from here on. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Aatrox's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Grandmaster at Arms' Armor/MR burst races World Ender's heal amp, so it is a coinflip — all-in only once his R (120s) is spent.

edits.before: Trinity Force is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on World Ender's cooldown.
edits.after: His healing item out-drains your first item — trade short, fight only while World Ender is down.

edits.before: Grandmaster’s Might stats win every extended duel from here on — build your teamfight around that. Aatrox carry threat: 8/10 — anti-heal stays core, shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.

edits.before: E to dodge his Q3 + autos
edits.after: E out of Infernal Chains — it grounds

notes: Level chart flipped as one atomic group: full phases[N].side and content win[N] proposed in pairs, matching the packet levelChart and the existing whys text, which already described Aatrox winning levels 2-5 and first item.
